Pidhaytsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Pidhaytsi is considered one of the oldest and best-preserved Jewish cemeteries in Ukraine. Its oldest documented surviving tombstone dates to 1630, though the Yizkor memorial book for Pidhaytsi mentions tombstones dated as early as 1420 that may once have stood here — it remains genuinely unclear whether these 15th-century stones simply did not survive, or whether this reflects local legend rather than history. Sabbatianism and Frankism found followers among Pidhaytsi's Jews in the 18th century, before Hasidism came to predominate by its end; Rabbi Shalom Lilienfeld founded a Talmud-Torah in 1905, and Itzhak-Isaac-Menahem Aichenstein (1879–1943) founded a Hasidic court in 1909. During the ghetto and labor camp's liquidation in early June 1943, prisoners were executed directly at this cemetery. Two synagogues, from the 16th and 19th centuries, were still being maintained as recently as the 1990s.
